title: Budgeting Your First Paychecks
summary: Learn how to build a simple spending plan around actual take-home pay, regular expenses, irregular costs, savings goals, and unexpected expenses.
objectives: Build a basic budget using simulated net income.
Distinguish fixed, variable, and occasional expenses.
Explain why savings and unexpected expenses should be considered before spending all available income.

vocab.def: A plan for how available income may be allocated across expenses, savings, and other goals.
An expense that tends to remain similar from one period to another.
An expense that can change from one period to another.
Money intentionally set aside to help handle unexpected expenses or financial disruptions.

sections.heading: Start with money you can actually use
sections.body: A practical budget starts with expected net income rather than gross earnings.

sections.heading: Separate needs, commitments, and flexible spending
sections.body: Housing, transportation, food, communication, savings, debt obligations, and personal spending can affect how much money remains available.

sections.heading: Not every expense happens every week
sections.body: Vehicle repairs, school expenses, clothing, annual fees, medical costs, gifts, or other irregular expenses can still affect a budget.

sections.heading: A budget is a plan that can change
sections.body: Income and expenses may change. A useful budget can be reviewed and adjusted instead of being treated as a permanent rule.

practice.prompt: A worker receives $1,200 in net income for the month and immediately plans to spend all $1,200. What is missing?
practice.answer: The plan should consider required expenses, savings goals, irregular costs, and unexpected expenses.

practice.prompt: Your transportation cost changes from week to week. Is it still part of the budget?
practice.answer: Yes. Variable expenses still need to be estimated and planned for.

quiz.question: What is the best starting point for a paycheck-based budget?
options: Money you hope to earn eventually

lab.objective: Build a simulated monthly spending plan using fictional net income, expenses, savings, and unexpected costs.

reflectionPrompt: What category would you want to plan for before spending your first paycheck?
